propositions: At search exhaustion, bounded fallback evidence currently banks met=false (evidence-of-absence) instead of distinguishing insufficient evidence, causing false FAIL verdicts on criteria whose evidence exists but was not reached within the window.

The fix introduces a tri-state verdict system: met (true/false) plus optional evidence_sufficient:false marker, so exhaustion is distinguishable from positive refutation and consumers can report insufficient evidence rather than unmet criteria.

The marker is framework-owned only (never model-facing); the widened fallback_record contract and new CriterionBank.record_insufficient route exhaustion through the marker path while preserving bare met=false as positive refutation.

Preserve-on-overwrite logic in harvest_structured_into_bank and merge_finalizer_with_bank ensures a prior entry's insufficient marker survives unless replaced by genuine refutation (bare met=false), and re-stamps every record from the authoritative bank entry.

All verdict consumers (schema validation, close_precheck refusal, _render_verdict_text, audit page, sidecar payload) must be marker-aware to report insufficient evidence + remediation (re-verify, cite evidence in comments) rather than unmet criteria guidance, preventing the anti-pattern of tagging code-verifiable criteria as operator-attested.

Extraction of completion_verdict_assembly.py extracted verdict-assembly functions to keep completion_banking.py under the 800 LOC cap while preserving the single chokepoint (reconcile_verdict) that derives top-level markers and routes both verdict kinds.
